extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting rebuttals to CVPR/ECCV (also reviewers and area chairs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing the one-page, anonymous author response (rebuttal) for CVPR/ECCV: required format, permitted and prohibited content, tone, writing process, and expectations for reviewers reading and requesting follow-up during the rebuttal phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and length
rubrics_metrics.description: The rebuttal is limited to a one-page PDF file. Responses longer than one page will simply not be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes responses where the margins and formatting are deemed to have been significantly altered; such responses will not be reviewed. Keep to the one-page PDF constraint exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: The rebuttal should be thorough, direct, and easy for the Reviewers and Area Chair (RACs) to follow; its purpose is to clarify and convince.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat rebuttal as a stage in deliberation: clarify misunderstandings, correct factual errors, and provide requested minor additional results. Aim for clarity and persuasion rather than comprehensive rewrites or introducing major new content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted content (What to include)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author rebuttal is meant to provide an opportunity to: Rebut factual errors; Supply additional information requested by the reviewers; Clarify misunderstandings; Provide minor additional results explicitly requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include focused clarifications and small pieces of additional data/illustration specifically asked for by reviewers. Be explicit about which reviewer comment you address and where changes will be made in the paper (if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited content (What NOT to include)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include: New contributions (theorems, algorithms, experiments) absent in the original submission and not specifically requested; Substantial new experiments; Personal attacks on reviewers; New related work (other than to address reviewer-flagged gaps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid introducing substantial novel technical material or large-scale experiments in the rebuttal. Keep tone professional and avoid any language that could be perceived as personal or combative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Be conversational. If a reviewer is wrong, do not say they're wrong. Instead, say 'there seems to be a misunderstanding' or 'perhaps the wording was unclear.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a conversational, non-combative tone to make responses easier for RACs to follow and less likely to be perceived as hostile. Acknowledge legitimate criticism gracefully rather than becoming defensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for writing rebuttals
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize and respond systematically: Itemize reviewer comments, group common concerns across reviewers, address each concern point-by-point, indicate where in the revised paper changes will be made, acknowledge legitimate criticism gracefully, and provide concrete evidence/data where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical steps: use a spreadsheet to track comments; explicitly map responses to reviewer points; show where text/figures will change in the paper; when possible, include concise evidence (numbers, small plots) rather than vague statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The rebuttal must maintain anonymity. It cannot include links to external material such as code, videos, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reveal author identity or link to external resources that could deanonymize the submission. Keep all supporting information within the one-page PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer request limits during rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may request clarifications, additional illustrations, or small experiments that could be reasonably run within the rebuttal phase with academic resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per a passed 2018 PAMI-TC motion, reviewers should not request substantial additional experiments for the rebuttal. Authors should comply with reasonable small requests but are not expected to perform large-scale new work at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer norms for reading rebuttals
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should read all rebuttals carefully, update their reviews to acknowledge addressed concerns, not raise new substantive criticisms in post-rebuttal phase, and engage in discussion with co-reviewers and AC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area chairs and reviewers are expected to incorporate rebuttal content into their evaluation and to focus post-rebuttal discussion on reconciliation and decision rather than introducing fresh major criticisms.
